claims.claim: GE Aerospace sits on a causal chain from air-travel/defense demand through engine deliveries and aftermarket uptime to constrained precision castings; acquiring CPP is a direct attempt to internalize a mission-critical casting bottleneck rather than merely add unrelated capacity.

The principal successor bottleneck is execution: casting ownership only creates resilience if qualification, integration and throughput convert into engine deliveries without worsening margin pressure.

falsifiers: CPP integration fails to improve constrained-part throughput or delivery cadence
capacity gains are offset by persistent margin degradation or new supplier bottlenecks

claims.claim: Strong Q2 orders, revenue and cash flow reduce the plausibility of a current demand-collapse thesis, but margin contraction prevents treating growth as frictionless execution.
The $11.75B CPP purchase concentrates capital-allocation and integration risk; acquisition of a bottleneck is not evidence that the bottleneck has already been solved.

risks.risk: Large acquisition price creates integration and return-on-capital risk.
Margin contraction shows mix, investment and inflation can absorb demand strength.

unknowns.unknown: Realized CPP synergies, qualification timing and post-close capacity economics remain forward-looking.

falsifiers: post-close throughput and delivery metrics fail to improve despite acquired capacity
integration costs or leverage materially impair cash generation
